title: Fibre localization of a Cartesian Grothendieck total category
statement:
Use the model-category and homotopy coherent localization conventions of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] and the infinity-category conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Fix an ordinary category $B$ and a strict contravariant diagram $F:B^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Cat}$, where each $F(b)$ has a model structure with weak equivalences $W_b$. Assume that for every $f:b\to c$ the functor $f^*:F(c)\to F(b)$ preserves all weak equivalences. Choose larger universes in which $B$, the fibres and their total category are small. Define the ordinary Cartesian Grothendieck total category $E$ to have objects $(b,X)$ with $X\in F(b)$, arrows $(b,X)\to(c,Y)$ pairs $(f,u)$ with $f:b\to c$ and $u:X\to f^*Y$, and composition $(g,v)(f,u)=(gf,f^*v\circ u)$. Let $W_E$ consist of those $(f,u)$ for which $f$ is an isomorphism and $u\in W_b$. Let $F_\infty:NB^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ be the diagram obtained by localizing every fibre and transition functor. Then there is a natural equivalence over $NB$
$$E[W_E^{-1}]_\infty\simeq\int_B F_\infty.$$
Here $N$ is the ordinary nerve and the right side is the Cartesian infinity-category of the diagram $F_\infty$: its fibre at $b$ is $F(b)[W_b^{-1}]_\infty$, its transport along $f$ is localized $f^*$, and its mapping space from $(b,X)$ to $(c,Y)$ is
$$\coprod_{f\in\operatorname{Hom}_B(b,c)}\operatorname{Map}_{F(b)[W_b^{-1}]_\infty}(X,f^*Y),$$
with composition and higher coherences induced by the localized diagram. The comparison restricts to fibre localization and takes $(f,u)$ to the composite of the localized $u$ and the Cartesian arrow $(b,f^*Y)\to(c,Y)$. For a coherent natural transformation $F_\infty\to G$, where $G:NB^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$, the induced map on Cartesian total infinity-categories exists and is an equivalence whenever every fibre component is an equivalence.

source.place: Haugseng, Rectification of enriched infinity-categories, Corollary 4.22 and Theorem 4.21, applied to opposite fibres and the opposite base; Theorem 4.6 and Remark 4.7 identify the relative nerve with unstraightening. Model categories are particular partial model categories as in Section 4.2. Read online, not archived. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical localization theorem.

proof.text: Work first in covariant notation. Put $C=B^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $H(c)=F(c)^{\mathrm{op}}$, with opposite model structures and opposite transition functors. Its ordinary opfibration total category $T$ is $E^{\mathrm{op}}$: arrows over $a:c\to d$ have components $a_!X\to Y$, where $a_!=H(a)$. Its weak equivalences $W_T$ are precisely arrows with invertible base and weak-equivalence component. The opposite model axioms follow by interchanging the two lifting/factorization systems, and every $a_!$ preserves weak equivalences by hypothesis. We shall prove the covariant localization statement for this diagram. By [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization], a locally Kan replacement of $L^H(T,W_T)$ presents the localization $\mathcal L$ and its mapping spaces, naturally in relative functors. The projection to $C$ carries $W_T$ to isomorphisms, hence induces $p:\mathcal L\to NC$ by that universal property. Concretely, composing each row of a hammock after inverting its leftward base isomorphisms gives a base arrow. Commutativity of its squares and the identity endpoint vertical maps show that all rows give the same arrow; column reduction preserves it and concatenation composes it. This defines a simplicial functor $L^H(T,W_T)\to C$, where $C$ has discrete mapping sets, extending the ordinary projection. For computations over $NC$ apply the functorial locally Kan replacement fixing discrete categories of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] to this functor; this retains a map of mapping spaces to the discrete sets $\operatorname{Hom}_C(c,d)$ and presents the projection $p$ above. Fix containing universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$ large enough that $C$, $T$, all slices, their hammock mapping simplicial sets, the locally Kan replacements, and (for the final clause) the values of the given diagram $G$ in this proof are $\mathcal U$-small; form their functor and fibration infinity categories in $\mathcal U'$. This is the size convention required when applying straightening below.

source.place: Section 4.2, Definition 4.13 and Corollary 4.15; agent slice-adjunction proof replacing the defective even-length reduction in Theorem 4.19 / Proposition 4.20.

proof.text: Fix $d\in C$ and form $T_d=(C_{/d})\times_C T$. Explicitly an object is $(\alpha:c\to d,X\in H(c))$; a morphism to $(\beta:c'\to d,X')$ is $(a,u)$ with $\beta a=\alpha$ and $u:a_!X\to X'$. Let $W_d$ consist of arrows whose underlying arrow in $T$ lies in $W_T$. There are functors $r_d:T_d\to H(d)$ and $j_d:H(d)\to T_d$ given by $r_d(\alpha,X)=\alpha_!X$, $r_d(a,u)=\beta_!u$, and $j_dY=(1_d,Y)$. Both preserve weak equivalences: for $r_d$ use preservation of weak equivalences by $\beta_!$; for $j_d$ the base is an identity. The arrow $\eta_{(\alpha,X)}:(\alpha,X)\to j_dr_d(\alpha,X)$ has base $\alpha$ and component $1_{\alpha_!X}$. Every arrow $(\alpha,X)\to j_dY$ is uniquely its composite with $j_d(v)$ for $v:\alpha_!X\to Y$. Thus $r_d\dashv j_d$, $r_dj_d=1$, the counit is the identity, and $r_d\eta=1$, $\eta j_d=1$, as strict natural identities. No model structure on $T$ or $T_d$ has been assumed or constructed.

source.place: Agent proof: explicit opfibration over the ordinary slice C/d; the factorization of arrows used in Proposition 4.20.

proof.text: Localize these relative functors using [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization], obtaining $R_d:\mathcal L_d\to H(d)_\infty$ and $J_d:H(d)_\infty\to\mathcal L_d$, where $\mathcal L_d=T_d[W_d^{-1}]_\infty$. The same universal property includes full functor categories, so the ordinary unit, after composing with localization, extends to a coherent transformation $\eta_\infty:1\to J_dR_d$; its uniqueness includes the mapping spaces of transformations. It also extends $r_dj_d=1$, $r_d\eta=1$, and $\eta j_d=1$ to their coherent identities. For $x\in\mathcal L_d$ and $y\in H(d)_\infty$, the maps of spaces $h\mapsto J_d(h)\eta_{\infty,x}$ and $k\mapsto R_d(k)$ give inverse equivalences between $\operatorname{Map}_{H(d)_\infty}(R_dx,y)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal L_d}(x,J_dy)$. Indeed the first composite is $h\mapsto hR_d(\eta_{\infty,x})=h$; the other is $k\mapsto J_dR_d(k)\eta_{\infty,x}=\eta_{\infty,J_dy}k=k$, by naturality and the two unit identities. These are homotopies of maps of mapping spaces, and the functor-category universal property makes them coherent and natural, rather than merely identities on components. In particular this proves a localized adjunction without any Quillen assumption on $r_d$ or $j_d$.

source.place: Agent proof from the full functor-category localization universal property; slice replacement for Proposition 4.20.

proof.text:
For $X\in H(c)$, $Y\in H(d)$ and $\phi:c\to d$, projection $T_d\to T$ induces an isomorphism of simplicial sets
$$L^H(T_d,W_d)((\phi,X),(1_d,Y))\cong L^H(T,W_T)(X,Y)_\phi.$$
Here the subscript is the inverse image of $\phi$ under the map to the discrete set of base arrows. To construct the inverse, take any reduced hammock on the right. In each row assign to every vertex over $c_i$ the arrow $\alpha_i:c_i\to d$ obtained by composing the remaining base arrows towards the final vertex $Y$, using the inverse base arrow whenever the horizontal arrow points left. These inverses exist because all leftward arrows are in $W_T$. Its first and last arrows to $d$ are $\phi$ and $1_d$. Every horizontal arrow over $a$ satisfies $\alpha_{i+1}a=\alpha_i$ (or the reversed equation for a leftward arrow), so lifts uniquely to $T_d$. For every vertical arrow over $v$, commutativity of the suffix of the hammock and the identity at $Y$ give $\alpha'_iv=\alpha_i$, so that arrow also lifts uniquely and remains in $W_d$. This constructs a unique hammock upstairs. Deleting/repeating rows, composing adjacent columns and deleting identity columns leave precisely the same suffix composites; thus lifting commutes with faces, degeneracies and reduction. These operations are the hammock operations specified by [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization]. That node and the mapping-space comparison of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] therefore identify the corresponding localized mapping spaces. Taking a single component over a discrete set preserves the weak equivalences here; it is also a homotopy fibre, by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] since maps of Kan spaces to a discrete set are Kan fibrations (a horn has constant base value).

source.place: Agent proof using full reduced hammocks of Definition 4.13 / Corollary 4.15, not the fixed four-arrow categories in Proposition 4.20.

proof.text:
Combining steps 3 and 4 with $x=(\phi,X)$ and $y=Y$ gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal L}(X,Y)_\phi\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{H(d)_\infty}(\phi_!X,Y).$$
The map from right to left is postcomposition with the fibre inclusion followed by precomposition with the image of the ordinary cocartesian arrow $\bar\phi:X\to\phi_!X$: in step 3 it is $h\mapsto J_d(h)\eta_x$, and projection sends $\eta_x$ to $\bar\phi$. Thus the comparison has the required map, not just the required homotopy type. It is natural in endpoint arrows and in relative maps of the diagrams: the suffix formula in step 4 commutes with these maps, and the unit and counit in step 3 are the stated natural transformations. All mapping spaces decompose as the coproduct of these components, because the base mapping set is discrete.

source.place: Agent deduction of the conclusion of Proposition 4.20 from the slice calculation; explicit comparison map.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-discrete-base-cocartesian-recognition] to $p:\mathcal L\to NC$ with $D_c=H(c)_\infty$, $i_c$ the localized fibre inclusion, and $u_{\phi,X}$ the image of the ordinary lift $\bar\phi_X$. Step 1's object-fixing hammock model represents every vertex by an original object. Identity lifts are identities and $\bar g_{\phi_!X}\bar\phi_X=\overline{g\phi}_X$ before localization, supplying the prescribed triangles. A lift of a base isomorphism lies in $W_T$, since its component is an identity, so its image is an equivalence. Step 5 supplies exactly the lemma's mapping equivalence $h\mapsto i_d(h)u_{\phi,X}$, with its endpoint naturality; it gives more than an equivalence of abstract homotopy types. Universes are fixed in step 1. The lemma therefore proves that these images are cocartesian, that $p$ admits a simplicial cocartesian representative, and that the canonical functors $J_c:H(c)_\infty\to\mathcal P_c:=\mathcal L\times_{NC}\{c\}$ are equivalences of intrinsic fibres.

source.place: Theorem 4.21, mapping-space criterion, with its mapping comparison supplied by steps 2-5 instead of the fixed-length zigzag argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-grothendieck-classifier-localization] to the same strict relative diagram $H$, its total category $T$, the cocartesian family $p$ of step 6, and $q:NT\to\mathcal L$ of step 1. Each $W_c$, the weak equivalences of the opposite model structure on $H(c)$, is a wide subcategory containing all isomorphisms (model-category weak equivalences contain the isomorphisms and are closed under composition by two-out-of-three), and the diagram's transitions preserve $W$ by hypothesis. The lemma's localization unit $\lambda_c$ and the hammock localization $H(c)_\infty$ of step 6 are both universal localizations of $(NH(c),W_c)$ (by [lem-coef-system-localization-universal] and [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization]), so they are identified by the unique comparison under $NH(c)$, and $J_c$ is transported along it. Step 6 proves that $q$ preserves the chosen ordinary lifts. Its fibre restriction is fibre localization followed by $J_c$, by the construction of $i_c$ in step 6. Thus every hypothesis of the cited lemma holds, including the intrinsic-fibre equivalences. It gives a coherent equivalence $H_\infty\simeq\operatorname{St}_{NC}(p)$ compatible with $q$ and the fibre localization units, hence an equivalence $\int_C H_\infty\simeq\mathcal L$ over $NC$. This includes the full classifying-diagram coherences and identifies the transport with localized $\phi_!$.

source.place: Corollary 4.22 and the classifying-diagram identification, proved here by the slice adjunction and straightening; opposite convention as in the item source.

proof.text: Reverse opposites to return to $B,F$. For any target infinity category $\mathcal D$, reversing all arrows and transformations gives $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal L^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal D)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal L,\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}}$. The full functor-category universal property of [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization], applied with target $\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}$, identifies the latter with $\operatorname{Fun}_{W_T}(NT,\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}}\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{W_T^{\mathrm{op}}}(NT^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal D)$. These equivalences commute with restriction, so $q^{\mathrm{op}}$ exhibits the localization of $(E,W_E)=(T^{\mathrm{op}},W_T^{\mathrm{op}})$. Taking opposites in the mapping-square characterization in [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] turns the cocartesian family into a Cartesian family. Its classifying diagram is $F_\infty$ by step 7, since its fibres are the opposite localizations and its transport is localized $f^*$. This proves the asserted comparison over $NB$.

source.place: Corollary 4.22 and the classifying-diagram identification, proved here by the slice adjunction and straightening; opposite convention as in the item source.

proof.text: The covariant mapping formula in step 5, after reversing source and target, is precisely $\coprod_{f:b\to c}\operatorname{Map}_{F(b)_\infty}(X,f^*Y)$. The ordinary factorization $(f,u)=(f,1)\circ(1,u)$ gives the required arrow action. Fibre restriction is the original localization functor by step 7's compatibility with its units. The construction uses functors and coherent transformations throughout, so composition and higher coherences are those of the localized diagram; their compatibility is part of step 7's comparison, not inferred just from agreement on objects or individual arrows.

source.place: Corollary 4.22 and the classifying-diagram identification, proved here by the slice adjunction and straightening; opposite convention as in the item source.

proof.text: Finally a coherent transformation $F_\infty\to G$ is a morphism in $\operatorname{Fun}(NB^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Cat}_\infty)$. Under the opposite form of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] it induces a functor over $NB$ preserving Cartesian edges. If its fibre components are equivalences, [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] says exactly that this coherent transformation is an equivalence in the functor infinity-category. Its image under the inverse straightening equivalence is then an equivalence of Cartesian fibrations, hence an equivalence of their total infinity-categories. This applies to arbitrary coherent transformations of the localized diagrams, with no strict natural transformation on the original model categories required.

source.place: Theorem 4.6 / Remark 4.7 interpreted as straightening; formal coherent transformation clause from the existing functor-category criterion.

proof_origin.place: Proof paragraph 2: coherent finite-coefficient mapping-complex adjunction. Agent slice-adjunction and full-hammock proof of the needed Grothendieck localization; Haugseng 4.19 even-length reduction is false, as detailed in report.md.
